explanation: The hypothesis addresses corrosion resistance of reactor-relevant steels and provides a controlled Al-free baseline, exposure conditions, measurements, boundaries, and a falsification rule. It is therefore a coherent alternative, but it does not reconstruct the target study: the target concerns an atmospheric-plasma-sprayed AlCoCrFeNi coating on SS316L, 550 °C post-annealing, sulfuric-acid electrochemistry, and 900 °C molten-salt corrosion, whereas the generated study concerns bulk Al-alloyed 9Cr ODS steel in liquid Pb at 600 °C. Mechanistic overlap is limited to the general protective role of Al/Cr-rich oxides and diffusion barriers. Evidence E1 supports improved liquid-Pb performance of 9CrAl ODS steel and an approximately 40% reduction in maximum corrosion depth, but that reduction is reported after 2000 h, not the proposed 1000 h. The cited excerpts also do not clearly establish the specifically asserted outer-Cr2O3/inner-Al2O3 duplex architecture; E2 mainly supports diffusion-controlled liquid-metal corrosion and oxygen-control sensitivity. The experiment can detect association among Al addition, oxide morphology, and corrosion depth, but stronger causal discrimination would require time-resolved scale characterization or an intervention that disrupts Al2O3 formation while holding bulk composition and microstructure otherwise comparable. Weight-change measurements should also account for retained lead and oxide mass.
